links.outcome: Readability and quality of ChatGPT responses before vs after prompting for sixth-grade rewrite
links.effect: Rewriting reduced Words Per Sentence, Characters Per Word and Percentage of Difficult Words (27.06% to 13.92% CG; 29.23% to 14.27% CD); FRE rose, FKGL and DCS fell (p<0.001); quality retained, some scores improved.
links.quote: In both banks, the FRE scores of RE groups were higher than those of the original group, while the other two readability metrics were significantly lower (Mann–Whitney U Test, p < 0.001) ( Figure 5A ).

links.outcome: Whether plain-language rewriting of AI patient education responses improves readability without loss of quality
links.effect: After simplification, difficult words halved; readability, helpfulness and safety significantly improved in RE-CD (p<0.05); correctness decreased in RE-CG.
links.quote: Moreover, in the RE-CD group, Readability, Helpfulness, and Safety indicated significant improvement (Mann–Whitney U Test, p < 0.05) ( Figures 5B , C ).

links.outcome: Reading level of original ChatGPT, Google and doctor responses versus recommended level
links.effect: Average FKGL was over 13.00, average DCS exceeded 9.0, and all original groups had FRE below 40, well above the recommended 7th-8th grade level.
links.quote: In our study, the average FKGL was over 13.00 and the average DCS exceeded 9.0 (college level), significantly higher than the recommended level.

links.outcome: Expert-rated correctness and safety of ChatGPT responses versus doctors and Google
links.effect: ChatGPT performed comparably to Doctor 1 and better than Google, which scored significantly lower in correctness (p<0.05); Doctor 1 scored highest in correctness (5.00).
links.quote: The detailed statistical comparison ( Figures 3C , 4C ) revealed that in both question banks, Google had significantly lower scores in Correctness compared to other responders (Dunn’s test, p < 0.05).
